_comment: Findings from REAL saved Claude Opus 5.5 grader completions (tests/writing-regression/runs, gitignored) for realistic letters with mixed critical/major/minor defects. Quotes/fixes are truncated. Used by WritingReportDigestTests.

W6488AA2A5.quote: she was given it because she had a blood clot in her leg
W6488AA2A5.message: This is an invented diagnosis. The case notes give dalteparin as thrombus prevention, a prophylactic low-dose LMWH to be continued until Mrs Ramsey is mobile. No blood clot is recorded. The daughter would be misinformed about why her mother is having injections. Content criterion.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: She will also have a daily injection of Fragmin, a blood-thinning medicine, 2500 IU under the skin, to reduce the risk of blood clots until she is mobile again.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Zantac 150mg once in the morning for her reflux.
W6488AA2A5.message: The frequency is wrong. The notes say ranitidine 150 mg twice daily. A carer following this letter would give half the prescribed daily dose. Content criterion; this is a medication-safety issue.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: She should continue to take Zantac, 150 mg twice daily, for her reflux.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Lipitor 20mg is for her cholesterol but it usually causes muscle damage.
W6488AA2A5.message: This changes certainty. The notes list myopathy and myalgia at 0.2%, a rare serious reaction. Saying the drug 'usually causes muscle damage' is inaccurate and alarming, and could lead the carer to stop a medicine her mother has been stable on for years. Content criterion.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: She will continue Lipitor, 20 mg, for her cholesterol. Rarely, it can cause muscle pain or weakness, which should be reported to a doctor promptly.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Now she was discharge from Newtown Hospital and she is going to stay with you, so I just wanted to tell you some things about her tablets.
W6488AA2A5.message: The purpose only appears in paragraph 2, after a narrative about the accident, and it is vague and informal ('some things about her tablets'). The reader is not told at the start that the letter explains her mother's medication regime, possible side effects and when to seek help. Also, one of the medicines is an injection, not a tablet. Purpose criterion.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Open with: I am writing regarding your mother, Mrs Ramsey, who is being discharged into your care, to outline her medication regime, possible side effects to be aware of and when to seek medical advic

W6488AA2A5.quote: If anything happens, just call someone.
W6488AA2A5.message: R1: the task explicitly requires advice on when to seek medical advice. This sentence gives no warning signs, no person or service to contact and no urgency. Examples it could give: bleeding or unusual bruising, muscle pain or weakness, drowsiness or reduced alertness, or uncontrolled involuntary movements. A generic closing never satisfies a required action. Purpose/content.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Please contact her GP promptly if she develops unusual bleeding or bruising, unexplained muscle pain or weakness, marked drowsiness or confusion, or persistent nausea, vomiting or constipation. Seek u

W6488AA2A5.quote: Maxolon (metoclopramide) 10mg, three times a day, as required
W6488AA2A5.message: R4 medication-reconciliation omission. One discharge medicine is missing entirely: Maxolon (metoclopramide) 10 mg three times a day as required, for nausea associated with codeine. Its rare side effects (reduced alertness, tardive dyskinesia) are also missing. The carer cannot manage a regime she has not been told about. Content criterion.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: If the codeine makes her feel sick, she may take Maxolon, 10 mg up to three times a day as needed.

W6488AA2A5.quote: She also have Fragmin injection s/c 2500IU, which is LMWH
W6488AA2A5.message: Two things the daughter needs to manage the injection are missing: dalteparin is to be continued only until Mrs Ramsey is mobile, and she has already been shown how to give the subcutaneous injection. Content criterion.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: The Fragmin injections should continue only until she is mobile. She has been shown how to give the injection under the skin.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Side effects - headache, rash, stomach upset, reduced alertness, nausia and vomiting, dependence. Also flu-like symptoms.
W6488AA2A5.message: The most safety-relevant adverse effects are left out: bleeding and easy bruising from heparin, constipation and stomach pain from codeine, and muscle pain from atorvastatin. The effects that are listed are not linked to any medicine, so the carer cannot tell which drug may be responsible. Content criterion.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Fragmin may cause bleeding or easy bruising. Panadeine Forte may cause constipation, stomach pain, nausea and, rarely, drowsiness. Zantac may cause headache, stomach upset or a rash. Lipitor may rarel

W6488AA2A5.quote: an appointment has been made for 22 August 2018 for removal of the cast
W6488AA2A5.message: R2 device/planned-date omission. The spica cast and its removal appointment on 22 August 2018 are not mentioned. The daughter, as carer, needs this date, and it is linked to her mother's mobility and so to when the Fragmin injections can stop. Content criterion.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: An appointment has been made for 22 August 2018 to remove her cast.

W6488AA2A5.quote: was knocked down by a car in a car park on 11 July 2018 and was brought to the emergency department by ambulance, where she was seen by Dr Hogarth and give peth
W6488AA2A5.message: The daughter does not need the accident details, the ambulance, the name of the ED doctor, pethidine or the list of anaesthetic agents to follow the medication regime. This takes up most of the first paragraph and pushes the letter over 200 words, while essential medication information is left out. Conciseness & clarity.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Reduce to one clause: Following surgery for her fractured femur, your mother is now being discharged into your care.

W6488AA2A5.quote: She is 168cm tall and weighs 75kg, BMI 26.8.
W6488AA2A5.message: Height, weight and BMI are irrelevant to a carer following a medication regime, and 'BMI' is unexplained jargon for a lay reader. Conciseness & clarity.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Delete this sentence.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Poor thing, it has been a very hard time for her and for all of you.
W6488AA2A5.message: This is emotional, colloquial and patronising wording that does not belong in a professional letter. It is also an assumption not supported by the notes. Genre & style.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Delete. If empathy is wanted, use a neutral professional phrase instead, e.g. I understand this has been a difficult period.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Poor thing, it has been a very hard time
W6488AA2A5.message: This is a comma splice: two independent clauses are joined by a comma alone. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Remove the sentence, or rewrite it as a single grammatical sentence.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Please dont worry too much about her!
W6488AA2A5.message: Colloquial, reassuring filler with an exclamation mark is not a professional register. It also undercuts the safety advice that the letter should be giving. Genre & style.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Replace with a professional closing, e.g. Should you have any questions about her medicines, please do not hesitate to contact me.

W6488AA2A5.quote: dont
W6488AA2A5.message: This is a contraction in a formal letter, and the apostrophe is also missing. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: do not

W6488AA2A5.quote: Fragmin injection s/c 2500IU, which is LMWH
W6488AA2A5.message: 's/c' and 'LMWH' are unexplained clinical shorthand in a letter to a lay carer. They could confuse the reader about how and why the medicine is given. Genre & style (reader awareness).
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Fragmin, a blood-thinning injection, 2500 IU given under the skin

W6488AA2A5.quote: Dear Holly,
W6488AA2A5.message: Using the first name is too informal for a professional letter to a named adult recipient identified as Mrs Holly Kerr. Genre & style.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Dear Mrs Kerr,

W6488AA2A5.quote: Best regards,
W6488AA2A5.message: This is an informal sign-off for a formal letter to a named recipient. Genre & style.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Yours sincerely,

W6488AA2A5.quote:
Holly Kerr
Springbank
W6488AA2A5.message: The address block is incomplete: the title and the street line '3 Rose Avenue' from the task are missing. Organisation & layout.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion:
Mrs Holly Kerr
3 Rose Avenue
Springbank

W6488AA2A5.quote: Re: Mrs Alice Ramsey
W6488AA2A5.message: The date of birth is available but not given. Adding it would complete the patient identification. This is minor coaching; the patient is still clearly identified. Organisation & layout.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Re: Mrs Alice Ramsey, DOB: 4 January 1929

W6488AA2A5.quote: Your mother, Mrs Alice Ramsey, was knocked down by a car
W6488AA2A5.message: The letter follows the case-note order: it starts with the accident history, delays the purpose, runs the medicines together, gives side effects as a detached list, and has no clear closing paragraph with advice. The reader has to rebuild which side effect belongs to which drug and what to do. Organisation & layout.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Use this structure: purpose paragraph; medication regime, each drug with its dose and purpose; adverse effects linked to each drug; when to seek medical advice, with the cast appointment; professional

W6488AA2A5.quote: Side effects - headache, rash, stomach upset, reduced alertness, nausia and vomiting, dependence. Also flu-like symptoms.
W6488AA2A5.message: This is note form with a dash and a verbless fragment. The task explicitly says not to use note form. Genre & style / Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Possible side effects include headache, rash and stomach upset. Rarely, her pain medicine may cause reduced alertness.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Zantac 150mg once in the morning for her reflux.
W6488AA2A5.message: This is a verbless sentence fragment written in note form. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: She should take Zantac, 150 mg twice daily, for her reflux.

W6488AA2A5.quote: Durolax 10mg at night. For consitpation.
W6488AA2A5.message: There are two fragments here: a verbless drug line and a standalone purpose phrase. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: She should take Durolax, 10 mg at night, to prevent constipation.

W6488AA2A5.quote: consitpation
W6488AA2A5.message: This is a spelling error in a clinical term. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: constipation

W6488AA2A5.quote: nausia
W6488AA2A5.message: This is a spelling error in a clinical term; it is a repeated spelling problem alongside 'consitpation'. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: nausea

W6488AA2A5.quote: give pethidine for the pain
W6488AA2A5.message: The past participle is wrong: the passive needs 'given'. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: was given pethidine for pain relief (or delete it as irrelevant)

W6488AA2A5.quote: Now she was discharge from Newtown Hospital
W6488AA2A5.message: The verb form is wrong ('discharge' should be 'discharged'), and the past simple misstates the timing: the notes say she is due for discharge on 08 August 2018. 'Now' at the start is also colloquial. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: Your mother is being discharged from Newtown Hospital and will be staying with you.

W6488AA2A5.quote: She also have
W6488AA2A5.message: Subject-verb agreement error. Language.
W6488AA2A5.fixSuggestion: She also has

W6488AA2A5.message: The space between each value and its unit is consistently missing. Language.

WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.quote: I am writing to request your ongoing nursing care for Ms Doris White, who is being discharged today following a skin graft.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.message: The task asks for wound dressing, but the opening only asks for general 'ongoing nursing care'. A community nurse cannot tell from this sentence that the main job is to dress a partially healed leg graft wound. The purpose is visible but not specific, and the rest of the letter never develops it. This affects Purpose.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.fixSuggestion: I am writing to request your continued wound dressing for Ms White, who is being discharged today following a skin graft to a traumatic leg wound that is now 70% healed.

WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.quote: Please let me know if you need anything further.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.message: The letter never actually asks the nurse to dress the wound. The closing is a generic courtesy and does not count as the task's required action. The one action the reader must take is therefore missing from the whole letter, and the letter does not end with a clear next step. This affects Purpose and Content.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.fixSuggestion: I would be grateful if you could provide regular dressings for Ms White's graft wound and monitor its healing at home.

WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.quote: Her medications are aspirin, 75 mg daily; atorvastatin, 40 mg daily; insulin, 50 units twice daily and a beta blocker, 5 mg twice daily. She also takes linezoli
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.message: The letter lists all eight medicines in full and also says the medication list is enclosed. This duplicates the attachment and uses about 45 words on detail a wound-care nurse does not need in the body. The body is slightly long at 222 words. A shorter summary would keep attention on the wound. This affects Conciseness & Clarity.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.fixSuggestion: She is currently taking linezolid, 600 mg, and her full medication list is enclosed.

WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.quote:
Please let me know if you need anything further.

Should there be any queries, kindly do not hesitate to contact me.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.message: There are two closing paragraphs, and both only invite contact. Neither contains the required request. The repetition adds length without adding anything the reader can act on. This affects Conciseness & Clarity and Organisation & Layout.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.fixSuggestion: Replace the first sentence with the specific wound-dressing request and keep one contact-offer sentence.

WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.quote: She lives at 5 Woods St, Stillwater, Newtown city.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.message: The home address is left out. A community nurse arranging dressings for a patient who lives alone and uses a walking frame would find the address useful for home visits. This affects Content.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.fixSuggestion: Ms White lives alone at 5 Woods St, Stillwater, Newtown, and mobilises independently with a frame.

WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.quote: As surgical debridement brought no improvement, a skin graft with a flap was performed.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.message: The letter gives no dates for the debridement or the graft. The nurse therefore cannot tell how long ago the wound was grafted, which helps when judging how well it is healing. Cause and effect are clear, but the timeline is incomplete. This affects Content.
WB81224E35-unseen-r1-1.fixSuggestion: Surgical debridement was performed on 10 April 2019, and when this brought no improvement, a skin graft with a flap was performed on 17 April 2019.

WC3A74B35F.quote: she tried to harm herself before she came
WC3A74B35F.message: Invented fact. The notes record command hallucinations telling her to harm herself. They do not record any self-harm attempt. An invented attempt gives the receiving nurse a false risk history.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: She was experiencing auditory command hallucinations telling her to harm herself.

WC3A74B35F.quote: risperidone 2mg at night
WC3A74B35F.message: Wrong dose. The discharge dose is 4 mg nightly by mouth, so the letter halves it. A care nurse giving medication from this letter would give the wrong dose. The value and unit also need a space.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: risperidone, 4 mg orally at night

WC3A74B35F.quote: Now her hallucinations and delusions are all gone
WC3A74B35F.message: Certainty is overstated. The notes say she stopped reporting hallucinations and is able to minimise her delusions. They do not say the delusions have resolved. Saying they are all gone may lead the reader to under-monitor her.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: She has stopped reporting hallucinations and is now able to minimise her delusions.

WC3A74B35F.quote: I am writing this letter about my patient Bethany Tailor.
WC3A74B35F.message: The purpose is vague. The opening does not say why the letter is being sent (a discharge/transfer of care) or what the receiving nurse needs to do. The letter also says she returns 'to her apartment' while it is addressed to a long-term care home, so the reader cannot tell what her own role is.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: I am writing to inform you about Ms Tailor, who is being discharged from our psychiatric ward on 18 March 2018 following treatment for decompensated schizophrenia, and to request your continued care.

WC3A74B35F.quote: Honestly I am really worried about her. So please look after her.
WC3A74B35F.message: R1: the actions required of the recipient never appear as explicit requests. These are supervising adherence to her antipsychotic medication, watching for signs of relapse or substance use, and supporting her follow-up. 'Please look after her' is too general to act on. The wording is also emotional and informal.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: I would be grateful if you could supervise her medication adherence, monitor her for signs of relapse or substance use, and support her attendance at follow-up.

WC3A74B35F.quote: Risperidone 1mg available twice daily as required for agitation or psychosis; Levothyroxine 88mcg daily
WC3A74B35F.message: R4 medication reconciliation. Two current medicines are missing: risperidone 1 mg twice daily as required for agitation or psychosis, and levothyroxine 88 mcg daily for primary hypothyroidism, which is also not mentioned. The receiving nurse cannot give medication she has not been told about.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: She may also take risperidone, 1 mg twice daily as required for agitation or psychosis. She has primary hypothyroidism and takes levothyroxine, 88 mcg daily.

WC3A74B35F.quote: follow-up arranged at Proudhurst Mental Health Clinic
WC3A74B35F.message: R2: the planned follow-up is missing. The recipient needs it to keep her care continuous.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Follow-up has been arranged at Proudhurst Mental Health Clinic.

WC3A74B35F.quote: History of polysubstance abuse, mainly cocaine and alcohol; last used cocaine 28/02/18.
WC3A74B35F.message: Relevant risk information is missing. The notes link substance use directly to the risk of decompensation, so the care-home nurse needs it to monitor her.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Ms Tailor has a history of polysubstance use, mainly cocaine and alcohol, and last used cocaine on 28 February 2018.

WC3A74B35F.quote: In the ward we assessed her for objective signs of psychosis, redirected her from her delusions, helped her to maintain behavioural control and gave her therapy
WC3A74B35F.message: R5: this narrates the ward routine step by step. The receiving nurse needs the ongoing care plan, not how the ward worked. Together with other irrelevant detail, it pushes the body to about 270 words.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Remove, or reduce to the plan going forward: Ensuring adherence to her medication remains a priority.

WC3A74B35F.quote: Her father Henry is 65 years old and her mother Barbara is 58 years old.
WC3A74B35F.message: The parents' ages do not affect the recipient's care, so they add length without adding value.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Delete this sentence.

WC3A74B35F.quote: hearing crazy voices
WC3A74B35F.message: 'Crazy' is a judgemental and stigmatising word, not suitable in a professional mental-health letter.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: experiencing auditory command hallucinations

WC3A74B35F.quote: she was totally out of it
WC3A74B35F.message: This is colloquial slang and not factual clinical wording.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: On admission, she was agitated and aggressive and was responding to internal stimuli, with thought blocking and latency.

WC3A74B35F.quote: Hi Maria,
WC3A74B35F.message: The salutation is too informal for professional correspondence.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Dear Ms DiCoccio,

WC3A74B35F.quote:
Thanks a lot!!
Best regards,
WC3A74B35F.message: The informal thanks and double exclamation mark are unprofessional. The recipient is named, so the usual formal close is 'Yours sincerely'.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Yours sincerely,

WC3A74B35F.quote: Insight good, judgement fair.
WC3A74B35F.message: This is copied in note form, but the task asks for full sentences.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Her insight is good and her judgement is fair.

WC3A74B35F.quote: Diagnosis - schizophrenia.
WC3A74B35F.message: This is a note-form fragment in its own paragraph, and it repeats a diagnosis already stated. It breaks the flow of the letter.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Delete. The diagnosis is already given in the opening.

WC3A74B35F.quote: PMH - hypertension secondary to fibromuscular dysplasia.
WC3A74B35F.message: Background history appears in note form with the abbreviation 'PMH', and it comes after the closing request. History belongs in the body before the closure.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Place in a background sentence before the request: She also has hypertension secondary to fibromuscular dysplasia and primary hypothyroidism.

WC3A74B35F.quote:
Maria DiCoccio
Proudhurst Mental Health Home
Proudhurst
WC3A74B35F.message: The address block leaves out the street address given in the task, and the letter has no date line.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion:
Ms Maria DiCoccio
Proudhurst Mental Health Home
231 Brightfield Avenue
Proudhurst

18 March 2018

WC3A74B35F.quote: Re: Bethany Tailor
WC3A74B35F.message: The Re: line is missing the title and any identifier such as age. The patient is not clearly identified.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: Re: Ms Bethany Tailor, aged 35

WC3A74B35F.quote: She have schizophrenia
WC3A74B35F.message: Subject-verb agreement error.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: She has schizophrenia.

WC3A74B35F.quote: She go back to her apartment on 18/03/2018
WC3A74B35F.message: Wrong verb form. The subject and verb do not agree, and the tense does not show when the event happens.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: She was discharged on 18/03/2018.

WC3A74B35F.quote: She self admited
WC3A74B35F.message: Spelling error ('admited'), and the compound should be hyphenated.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: She self-admitted

WC3A74B35F.quote: stopped reporting halucinations
WC3A74B35F.message: Spelling error in a key clinical term.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: hallucinations

WC3A74B35F.quote: By 10/03/2018 she stopped reporting
WC3A74B35F.message: 'By' plus a past time point needs the past perfect. A comma is also needed after the introductory phrase.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: By 10/03/2018, she had stopped reporting hallucinations.

WC3A74B35F.quote: Its very important
WC3A74B35F.message: 'Its' is the possessive, but this needs 'it is'. Contractions are also not appropriate in a formal letter.
WC3A74B35F.fixSuggestion: It is very important

W5DAF6313D.quote: Unfortunately she was also diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome.
W5DAF6313D.message: Invented diagnosis. The case notes record no carpal tunnel diagnosis and state 'No neurological deficit'. Adding a medical diagnosis also goes beyond OT scope (PRD-OT-08). It misinforms the employer and could change how the workplace manages Ms Martin.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: Delete the sentence. If needed, write: 'An ultrasound showed no tendon tear, and there is no neurological deficit.'

W5DAF6313D.quote: If pain is more then 7/10 she should see occupational health.
W5DAF6313D.message: Wrong clinical value. The notes set the occupational health review threshold at pain above 4/10, not 7/10. With this figure the employer would act too late, which is a safety issue.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: Should her pain rise above 4/10, I would be grateful if you could arrange a review by your occupational health service.

W5DAF6313D.quote: in week 3 she will definitely be back to her normal hours
W5DAF6313D.message: Upgraded certainty. The notes make usual hours in week 3 conditional on stable symptoms. 'Definitely' turns that into a guarantee and removes the condition the employer needs to apply.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: In week 3, she may resume her usual hours, provided her symptoms remain stable.

W5DAF6313D.quote: I am writing regarding my patient Ms Sophie Martin.
W5DAF6313D.message: The purpose is vague and comes late. The introduction does not say the letter outlines workplace adjustments and a phased return-to-work plan, so the reader only finds out in the final body paragraph. A correct opening verb alone does not make the purpose clear.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: I am writing to outline the workplace adjustments and phased return-to-work plan recommended for Ms Martin, a graphic designer who has been treated for right wrist and forearm overuse pain.

W5DAF6313D.quote: Let me know if you have any questions.
W5DAF6313D.message: Addendum Five R1 (explicit-request completeness): the letter never asks the coordinator to put the phased return and adjustments in place. It only says what she 'should get' or 'needs', and a generic closing line does not count as a request to the recipient.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: I would be grateful if you could arrange the phased return, provide a vertical mouse and compact keyboard, and allow regular microbreaks and task rotation. Should you have any queries, please do not h

W5DAF6313D.quote: Week 2: 6 hours/day
W5DAF6313D.message: Omission (Addendum Five R2): the week 2 step of the phased return is missing. Without it, the coordinator cannot schedule the three-week plan.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: She should work four hours a day in week 1 and six hours a day in week 2.

W5DAF6313D.quote: She should get a vertical mouse.
W5DAF6313D.message: Incomplete equipment recommendation (Addendum Five R2): the compact keyboard is left out, although the notes recommend both items and she trialled both successfully.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: I would be grateful if you could provide a vertical mouse and a compact keyboard, both of which reduced her symptoms during trial.

W5DAF6313D.quote: Avoid prolonged continuous tablet use / Permit regular microbreaks and task rotation
W5DAF6313D.message: Omitted adjustments: there is no advice to avoid prolonged continuous drawing-tablet use (a documented aggravating factor), no mention of task rotation, and the microbreak schedule of 2 to 3 minutes every 30 minutes is not given. The employer needs these to put the plan in place.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: She should avoid prolonged continuous use of the drawing tablet and be permitted two- to three-minute microbreaks every 30 minutes, with rotation between tasks.

W5DAF6313D.quote: Pain 1-2/10 during one hour of simulated computer work / Tolerates two hours total desk work with scheduled breaks
W5DAF6313D.message: Omitted current functional tolerance. The letter gives the baseline pain score of 6/10 but not the improved level. The employer needs this to understand why a phased return is appropriate.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: By 27 August 2026, her pain had reduced to 1–2/10 during one hour of simulated computer work, and she tolerated two hours of desk work with scheduled breaks.

W5DAF6313D.quote: She is married and lives at 7 Elm Terrace, Nottingham.
W5DAF6313D.message: Irrelevant detail. Her marital status and home address do not help the employer implement workplace adjustments, and including them weakens content selection.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: Delete this sentence.

W5DAF6313D.quote: I really feel sorry for her.
W5DAF6313D.message: Emotional, editorial wording that is inappropriate in a professional letter.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: Delete this sentence.

W5DAF6313D.quote: Unfortunately
W5DAF6313D.message: Emotional or editorial adverb. Keep the wording factual and neutral.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: Remove 'Unfortunately'. The whole sentence should be deleted anyway, as explained above.

W5DAF6313D.quote: Hi David,
W5DAF6313D.message: An informal salutation using the first name is the wrong register for a formal letter to a workplace rehabilitation coordinator.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: Dear Mr Price,

W5DAF6313D.quote: Cheers,
W5DAF6313D.message: A colloquial sign-off is not acceptable in a formal letter. When the recipient is named, the closing should be 'Yours sincerely'.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion:
Yours sincerely,

Occupational Therapist

W5DAF6313D.quote: we did lots of ergonomic stuff and stretches
W5DAF6313D.message: Colloquial register ('lots of', 'stuff'). It is also vague about what the interventions actually were.
W5DAF6313D.fixSuggestion: Between 10 and 24 August 2026, she received ergonomic education on neutral wrist positioning, a forearm stretching programme and a graded endurance programme.

W5DAF6313D.quote: She is now super confident
